before.name: 2890 BC: Akkadian language names are recorded from about this time period

after.name: c. 2600–2500 BC: Early Akkadian words and names in writing; dates approximate

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The 29th-century overview asserts names were recorded about 2890 without an individual citation, but the linked Akkadian article places early names in the mid-third millennium and Oxford research places early syllabic evidence for Akkadian words and proper names at Fara and Tell Abu Salabikh between 2600 and 2500. Another Wikipedia first-written-language list gives c.2800 at Tell Harmal, whose article describes an Old Babylonian site; this apparent inconsistency needs separate verification. The new one-year slot is a regional reference to the Oxford period, not a proved first date or continuous use and not an exact place for any tablet. Later king-list copies do not establish the date they were written.
r2SourceEvidence.date_precision: Approximate period reference; not a verified exact-year writing event.
r2SourceEvidence.location_precision: Regional gameplay reference, not the place of a particular inscription.

before.name: First extant evidence of written Akkadian language

after.name: c. 24th century BC: Texts fully written in Akkadian; date approximate

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: The old statement claimed the first extant evidence of written Akkadian was 2400, contradicting the earlier-attested words and names. The Akkadian article says fully Akkadian texts begin to appear from about the 24th century BC. This slot is an approximate century reference, not the exact date of a first document; region and radius are gameplay settings.
